title: Who owns the shared future?
lines: A community can build a name together while one owner retains the power to sell its future.
Decentralised Brands asks whether the people who build that identity could also share control over its future.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Keep several contributors connected to one recognizable name, with the decision point visibly separate.
voiceDirections: Speak with quiet indignation; give gentle emphasis to sell its future. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.
Speak with curious hope; give gentle emphasis to share control. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: A name becomes a promise
lines: The book begins with brands as promises that let strangers trust something beyond a single person.
From guild marks to digital platforms, a name can carry memory, belonging, and practical dependence.

title: The powers behind participation
lines: That makes control over the name more consequential than a question of logos or marketing.
The inquiry explores who can change the rules, remove members, preserve records, and make leaving possible.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Reduce governance choreography to one rule change and one possible exit, without suggesting that a vote resolves ownership.

Start with the promise behind the name, then follow the power to decide what it becomes.
